narrative:
The model estimates a 47% chance that you will leave your current job. Because this probability is high enough to flag a risk of departure, the organization has decided not to offer you the promotion at this time.

Three aspects of your profile most strongly shaped this outlook. First, having received other job offers while working here was the single biggest factor pushing the prediction toward leaving. Employees who get external opportunities are far more likely to depart than those who do not. Second, the fact that you have already spent 6–10 years in this organization pulled the prediction in the opposite direction; most people the model expects to stay have shorter tenure here. Third, your overall career experience of 6–10 years also nudged the prediction upward, as employees predicted to remain tend to have either less or considerably more total experience.

Taken together, the combination of attractive outside options and your mid-career stage outweighed the stabilizing effect of your time already invested with the company. The organization should therefore focus on understanding what would make staying more appealing to you, while you may wish to reflect on whether your current role still matches your longer-term goals. Addressing these points openly could either reduce the risk of departure or clarify a mutually beneficial next step. (218 words)
